theme: Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 32. Paul quotes the first two verses in Romans 4:7-8. Read it as David’s testimony of what it feels like to be justified, and notice the difference between hiding sin and confessing it.
settingTheScene: Psalm 32 is a psalm of David, called a “Maskil,” which means a teaching psalm. It is traditionally linked to David’s sin with Bathsheba and the long months of silence before Nathan confronted him (2 Samuel 11 to 12). It is one of the seven penitential psalms. Augustine loved it so much that he had it written on the wall beside his bed when he was dying. Paul read it in Romans 4 as proof that David knew the blessing of being counted righteous apart from works.
observation: “Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered” (v. 1).
“Blessed is the man against whom the LORD counts no iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no deceit” (v. 2).
“For when I kept silence, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long” (v. 3).
“For day and night your hand was heavy upon me; my strength was dried up as by the heat of summer” (v. 4).
“I acknowledged my sin to you, and I did not cover my iniquity” (v. 5).
“I said, I will confess my transgressions to the LORD, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin” (v. 5).
“I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with my eye upon you” (v. 8).
“Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but steadfast love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD” (v. 10).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with a double beatitude: “Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man against whom the LORD counts no iniquity.” Three words for sin appear: transgression (rebellion), sin (missing the mark), and iniquity (twistedness). Three words for forgiveness answer them: forgiven (lifted away), covered, and not counted. Paul will pick up this last phrase, “counts no iniquity,” as the very meaning of justification. Notice that the blessing is not for the one who has never sinned, but for the one whose sin is dealt with.

Then David tells his story. He kept silence, hiding his sin. The result was physical and spiritual misery: his bones wasted away, he groaned all day, and God’s hand was heavy on him day and night. His strength dried up like a field in summer. Unconfessed sin is a heavy load, and the conscience is God’s instrument to press us toward him. Many people have lived with the weight of what they will not admit.

Then the turn: “I acknowledged my sin to you, and I did not cover my iniquity; I said, I will confess my transgressions to the LORD, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin.” The sequence is short. David said he would confess, and God forgave. The speed of God’s forgiveness is striking. There is no penance or delay. The result is relief and safety: in a time of distress the rising waters will not reach him. The LORD becomes a hiding place.

God speaks in verse 8: “I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with my eye upon you.” Forgiveness leads to guidance. And then a warning not to be like a horse or mule that needs bit and bridle to stay near. God would rather lead by relationship than force.

The psalm ends with a call to joy: “Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, you righteous, and shout for joy, all you upright in heart!” For Christians, the foundation of this joy is clearer than it was for David. Our sin was not simply passed over; it was covered by the blood of Christ. The one against whom the Lord counts no sin is the one who is in Christ.
connection: Romans 4:6-8 quotes verses 1-2. 2 Samuel 12:13 records Nathan’s word, “The LORD has put away your sin.” Psalm 51 is David’s longer prayer after the same sin. Proverbs 28:13 says whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper. 1 John 1:5-10 teaches that if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive. James 5:16 tells us to confess to one another. Hebrews 4:16 invites us to the throne of grace. Psalm 103:10-12 says he removes our transgressions as far as the east is from the west.
application:
Spend a few minutes confessing specific sins to the LORD. Name them. Then thank him for forgiving.

If you are hiding something from God or from a trusted friend, bring it into the light.

Read the last verse aloud as a call to joy.
prayerPrompts: Acknowledge your sin to God without covering it.
Thank him for the forgiveness that makes you blessed.
Ask him to be your hiding place.
